_note: Terrain height grids for the elevation correction. One file per map.
Heights are metres above each map's own lowest sample. The source
height field has no usable absolute datum -- it sits some 900 m below
anything a player would call an altitude -- but it is internally
consistent, and only differences between two points are ever used.
Sampling: Landscape collision height field, 2 m spacing, taken every
4th vertex (8 m). Bilinear interpolation against the full 2 m data is
off by 0.13 m on average and 0.45 m at the 95th percentile.
File format: lzma stream -> uint16 little-endian zigzag residuals,
row-major, ny rows of nx. Each sample predicts its left neighbour,
the first of each row predicts the row above:
Row 0 is the lowest game Y, column 0 the lowest game X:
game_x = x0 + j * step_units,  game_y = y0 + i * step_units
